title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial
desc: Nature Medicine, Published online: 08 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04787-8 As presented at the 2026 AHA Scientific Sessions, a cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial showed that semaglutide significantly improved cardiac structure and function, including left atrial reservoir strain and left ventricular filling dynamics, in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity.

title: Wrist photoplethysmography encodes dietary information
desc: Whether wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) encodes dietary information remains unknown. We trained a language model on 1.1M meals to align PPG with meal descriptions. Near-meal PPG carries a meal-specific signal beyond individual traits; predictability decreases farther from meals. This transfers to dietary tasks: PPG increases AUC by 11% for a caloric-intake proxy and satiety across held-out and independent cohorts. Wearable PPG may augment text-based logging, compensating for brief descriptions.

desc: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Medical Image Analysis, Volume 116 Author(s): Haoran Li, Yuxin Lin, Huan Wang, Xiaoling Luo, Qi Zhu, Jiahua Shi, Huaming Chen, Bo Du, Johan Barthelemy, Zongyan Xue, Jun Shen, Yong Xu

title: Multimodal AI in Oral Cancer: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review.
desc: [Healthcare technology letters] Oral cancer presents significant diagnostic and prognostic challenges, often due to late-stage detection and tumour heterogeneity. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML), offer promising solutions by integrating multimodal biomedical data. This PRISMA-guided systematic review evaluates over 82 studies from 2015 to 2025 that apply convolutional neural networks, transformers and graph neural networks to oral cancer, using combinations of histopathology, radiology, genomics and clinical data. Results indicate that multimodal AI models consistently outperform unimodal approaches in diagnostic accuracy, AUC and survival prediction. Architectures employing attention mechanisms, graph embedding and fusion transformers demonstrate superior performance in tasks such as early lesion detection and treatment outcome modelling. Despite these advances, challenges persist in generalisability, data standardisation and clinical validation. Multimodal AI thus represents a paradigm shift toward precision oncology in oral cancer, warranting further research focused on interpretability, prospective validation and ethical clinical deployment.

title: AI-Assisted Differentiation of Pancreatic Cystic Lesions Using EUS Images and Clinical Features
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Ruijin Hospital; conditions: Pancreatic Mucinous Cystic Neoplasm, Pancreatic Serous Cystic Neoplasm, Pancreatic Pseudocyst; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 400; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Pancreatic mucinous cystic neoplasms (MCNs), serous cystic neoplasms (SCNs), and pancreatic pseudocysts (PPCs) often exhibit overlapping imaging features on endoscopic ultrasound (EUS). However, these conditions require different clinical management strategies. Accurate differentiation is therefore important for appropriate treatment planning. This study aims to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) model that integrates EUS images and clinical features to differentiate MCNs, SCNs, and PPCs. The study is designed as an ambispective observational diagnostic study consisting of retrospective model development, prospective temporal validation, and a reader study involving EUS physicians. Approximately 400 adult patients with confirmed MCN, SCN, or PPC will be included. Retrospective clinical data and EUS images will be used for model development and internal validation. After model development is completed, newly diagnosed patients will be prospectively enrolled to independently evaluate the diagnostic performance of the model. The primary outcome is the patient-level macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (macro-AUROC) for three-class classification in the prospective validation cohort. Secondary outcomes include diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, calibration, clinical net benefit, and the performance of EUS physicians with and without AI assistance. This study is expected to provide evidence for the potential clinical value of AI-assisted differentiation of pancreatic cystic lesions. No additional invasive procedures or study-specific treatments will be performed.

title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
desc: Language models are accurate on most long-arithmetic problems, but their accuracy is estimated on samples and carries no guarantee for an unseen input; tool use is exact but moves the computation outside the network. We show that exactness at all input lengths becomes a finite, checkable property of a network when each of its steps reads only a bounded view of an external working memory. In Sketchpad, Qwen3.5-0.8B with a low-rank adapter executes arithmetic procedures on a rendered sheet. Each forward pass reads a three-cell view and emits one step: a digit, a carry or borrow, and the next operation. A fixed runtime moves the view and writes no digit of a result. We prove in Lean that the model is then exact on all inputs of any length if and only if it is exact on the finite set of views the runtime presents, that no finite test suffices when steps also read earlier steps, and that the guarantee tolerates bounded numerical perturbation and extends to compositions of procedures. All 2,446 views pass on the deployment device, a laptop GPU running the model in a web browser. The certified model performs signed addition and subtraction, long multiplication and division, square roots and greatest common divisors at arbitrary length. It solved 200 of 200 pre-registered problems in the browser, and 220 of 220 sums of up to 1,000 digits and products of up to 20 digits, of which GPT-6.1 Sol, the strongest of ten other models, solved 217. A symbolic runtime built on these procedures solves, expands and factors polynomials with every number computed by the model, and a multiplicative gate on the adapter recovers the base model exactly when the sheet is not in use.

title: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery in Clinical Data
desc: Automated scientific discovery has the potential to advance understanding of disease mechanisms and accelerate identification of early disease markers. Manual data annotation is infeasible at population scale, motivating methods that automatically extract pre-defined phenotypes in multimodal and unstructured clinical data. Such pre-defined feature sets determine and limit which associations these approaches can discover. This limitation extends to agentic AI systems that use these tools to query population-scale data. In contrast, foundation models (FMs) trained on large volumes of clinical data can perform tasks beyond their training objectives. This suggests their latent embeddings may represent novel or unexplored features that could yield insights into disease mechanisms, yet such latent features remain difficult to interpret. To address this challenge, we introduce Glyph, an automated multistage framework that extracts features from multimodal and unstructured clinical data using FMs and sparse autoencoders, interprets them as coded clinical concepts, and evaluates their value for clinical scientific discovery. We applied Glyph to abdominal CT volumes, CT radiology reports and laboratory measurements from 41,628 patients across different institutions. We identified 397 predictive concepts supported by 4,463 Bonferroni-significant associations. Moreover, a majority of discovered associations were automatically reproducible in held-out cohorts across different sites. Glyph concepts provided complementary associations to literature-derived markers, leading to gains in predictive power. We envision that interpretability can extend beyond a mechanistic understanding of neural networks to connecting implicitly learned features with clinical knowledge and establishing their significance for patient outcomes. We release Glyph at https://github.com/StanfordMIMI/Glyph.

title: Methodological Adherence, Reporting Completeness, and Risk of Bias in AI-Assisted Systematic Reviews: A Matched Meta-Research Study
desc: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to accelerate systematic reviews that inform clinical practice and policy. However, evidence on the methodological adherence, reporting completeness, and risk of bias of completed AI-assisted reviews is limited. Objective: To compare methodological adherence, reporting completeness, and risk of bias between published systematic reviews with reported AI assistance and matched reviews with no reported AI use, and to assess AI-use transparency. Methods: We conducted a matched-cohort meta-research study of English-language, peer-reviewed health systematic reviews. AI-assisted reviews published during 2023--2025 were matched 1:2 to reviews with no reported AI use using individualized MEDLINE searches targeting publication timing, clinical domain, review type, and meta-analysis status. When more than two eligible comparators were available, two were randomly selected. AI assistance was defined as reported use during searching, screening, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, evidence synthesis, or substantive drafting. Full texts and supplementary materials were examined to classify reported AI use. The primary outcome was a prespecified modified 13-item AMSTAR-2 methodological-adherence score (range 0 -- 13; noninferiority margin &-1 point). Secondary outcomes included PRISMA 2020 reporting completeness and ROBIS risk of bias; AI-use transparency was assessed descriptively. Adapted 13-item AMSTAR-2 confidence categories were summarized descriptively, while critical- and noncritical-domain adherence was examined in exploratory adjusted analyses. Multivariable regression models adjusted for journal impact tier, funding reporting, formal review-group affiliation, review-team size, and review-question type, using cluster-robust standard errors by matched set. Sensitivity analyses included matched-set fixed-effects models. The study was registered on the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/Q5JRW). Results: The cohort included 231 systematic reviews: 77 AI-assisted and 154 with no reported AI use. Mean 13-item AMSTAR-2 scores were 7.58 and 9.63, respectively. In multivariable-adjusted analyses, AI-assisted reviews scored 1.64 points lower (95% CI &-2.37 to &- 0.91); noninferiority was not demonstrated. PRISMA adherence was estimated to be 4.7 percentage points lower among AI-assisted reviews in primary adjusted analyses (95% CI &-8.9 to &-0.6) and 6.4 points lower in matched-set fixed-effects

title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
desc: Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

title: Mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence in healthcare: a systematic review.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. This systematic review synthesized the classical and emerging mathematical foundations underpinning healthcare AI and examined major methodological and application trends. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies published between January 2016 and June 30, 2026, were identified through systematic searches of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE, with searches conducted using Harzing's Publish or Perish v8 where applicable. Bibliometric analysis was performed using VOSviewer, while methodological quality was assessed using an adapted JBI-based framework and AMSTAR-2 for systematic reviews. Of 653 records identified, 147 studies met the eligibility criteria. Non-mutually exclusive mathematical-domain coding identified linear algebra in 100/147 studies (68.0%), calculus and optimization in 91/147 (61.9%), and probability and statistics in 79/147 (53.7%), highlighting their roles in data representation, learning, optimization, inference, uncertainty quantification, and validation. A separate mutually exclusive classification of dominant methodological themes identified explainable and trustworthy AI in 24/147 studies (16.3%), statistics and learning theory in 23/147 (15.6%), probability and Bayesian methods in 23/147 (15.6%), calculus and optimization in 19/147 (12.9%), and linear algebra in 15/147 (10.2%). Radiology and medical imaging were the leading healthcare application (24.3%), while classification and diagnosis were the most frequent clinical task (17.1%). Overall, healthcare AI is supported by an interconnected mathematical ecosystem. Emerging approaches, including graph neural networks, Transformers, and quantum machine learning, require stronger external validation, standardized benchmarking, and rigorous evaluation for reliable clinical translation.

title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted Primary Care for Influenza Vaccination Among Chronic Patients in China (AIPC-Flu)
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Fudan University; conditions: Influenza Vaccination; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 1300; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether an AI-assisted primary care intervention can increase influenza vaccination uptake among patients with chronic diseases and to assess the cost-effectiveness and potential for implementing the intervention in routine primary care. The main questions it aims to answer are: 1. Does the AI-assisted primary care intervention increase influenza risk perception, influenza vaccine literacy, vaccine confidence, intention to receive influenza vaccination, and influenza vaccination uptake among patients with chronic diseases? 2. Is the AI-assisted primary care intervention cost-effective compared with conventional health education? 3. Is the AI-assisted primary care intervention acceptable, feasible, and potentially sustainable for influenza vaccination promotion? Researchers will compare patients with chronic diseases who receive the AI-assisted primary care intervention with those who do not receive it to determine whether the intervention improves patients' literacy, confidence, intention, and uptake of influenza vaccination. Participants will: 1. Be recruited and randomly assigned to the intervention group or control group. Participants in the intervention group will have access to an AI assistant for influenza vaccine-related information and will receive an influenza vaccination recommendation from primary care physicians, while participants in the control group will receive routine health education. 2. Complete a survey questionnaire assessing patients' influenza risk perception, influenza vaccine literacy, vaccine confidence, and intention to receive influenza vaccination. 3. Have their influenza vaccination uptake assessed at the end of the trial.

title: Hemodynamic effects of semaglutide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial
desc: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide improves symptoms in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) through unclear mechanisms. Here, in this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 81 patients (47 women) with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) or placebo for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in invasively measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), a direct measure of cardiac congestion, during low-intensity exercise. Additional mechanistic outcomes included other hemodynamic measures and hemodynamic HFpEF remission (defined as normal PAWP under conditions of both rest and exercise at 52 weeks). At baseline, PAWP was 17.5 ± 4.3 mmHg at rest and 31.7 ± 5.2 mmHg during exercise. After 52 weeks, the mean change in PAWP during exercise was −9.8 (95% confidence interval (CI): −11.3 to −8.2) mmHg with semaglutide and +0.9 (95% CI: −1.3 to 3.0) mmHg with placebo (estimated difference, −10.6 mmHg; 95% CI: −13.3 to −8.0; P < 0.0001). As compared to placebo, semaglutide also decreased resting PAWP (estimated difference, −7.1 mmHg; 95% CI: −9.8 to −4.4; P < 0.0001), and semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission (53.7% versus 7.4%, odds ratio = 14.1, 95% CI: 3.0−134.6, P < 0.001). The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05371496.

title: Next-Generation Cancer Nanovaccines: Reprogramming the Tumor Microenvironment from Rational Design Toward Clinical Translation.
desc: [International journal of nanomedicine] Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for inducing durable and tumour-specific immune responses; however, their clinical efficacy remains limited by poor antigen immunogenicity, inefficient delivery, tumor heterogeneity, and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in nanotechnology have expanded opportunities for the rational engineering of multifunctional nanoparticle (NP) platforms that can protect therapeutic cargo, enhance antigen presentation and lymphatic transport, co-deliver immunostimulatory adjuvants, and potentially improve immune modulation while reducing systemic exposure. This narrative review provides an overview of next-generation cancer nanovaccines, including lipid-, polymer-, peptide-, inorganic-, biomimetic-, theranostic, in situ-, and stimuli-responsive platforms, with emphasis on their physicochemical design principles, mechanisms of immune activation, and interactions with the TME. Particular attention is given to strategies targeting tumor -associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and tumor cells to support dendritic-cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell activation, and anti-tumor immunity. Emerging personalized approaches, including neoantigen- and autologous cell-based nanovaccines, mRNA vaccine platforms, and combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors, are also discussed. In addition, we examine the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational immunology in neoantigen prioritization, nanoparticle formulation optimization, immunogenicity prediction, and patient-specific vaccine design. Despite encouraging preclinical findings, most cancer nanovaccine platforms remain at the preclinical or early clinical stage, and translation is limited by tumor heterogeneity, variable immune responses, long-term safety and biodistribution concerns, manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory requirements. Overall, the integration of nanotechnology, immunology, precision medicine, and AI offers considerable potential to advance personalized cancer vaccination, but broader clinical validation and standardized manufacturing and evaluation frameworks are required before these platforms can achieve routine clinical application.

title: Automated Vetting and Protocolling of MRI Examinations
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Edozie Iweka; conditions: Analysis of Retrospectively Collected MRI Referral Data; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 900000; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Background Vetting and assigning of protocols to MRI scan requests are usually carried out by radiologists and radiographers. This way is both time-consuming and prone to error. Recent improvements in Artificial Intelligence (Al) like Large Language Models (LLMs) are better at processing human language. It could be used to improve tasks like image reporting and assigning protocols in radiology. Approach Firstly, I will find out about the delays in the way this is currently done. I will use a survey to find out the perceptions of radiologists to both the current process and the proposed Al intervention. I will then use an LLM to undertake referral and protocol tasks. I will compare its performance to the performance of clinical specialists and established guidelines. I will present the explanation reports to radiologists and ask them if they can be understood and whether they can be trusted as clinically reliable. Impact My research could help reduce the workload and time radiologists spend dealing with scan requests. The findings will help design future research to consider application in real clinical settings.

title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
desc: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. Across 69 organ-demographic combinations, demographic attributes were broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group, and 0.662 for self-reported race, and substantial variation across organs. Demographic-class balancing produced relatively small changes in performance, while evaluation within diagnosis-text clusters showed modest attenuation. Under training with diagnosis-based grouping, demographic-associated signals remained detectable across multiple organs, including sex in gastric tissue (AUROC 0.865), age group in breast (0.816), and self-reported race in skin (0.728). Literature-guided analysis of these settings generated candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations for further investigation. Together, these findings provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology, informing investigations of its sources, assessments of potential shortcut learning, and the development of more interpretable computational pathology models.

title: Figure format and the accuracy of AI-assisted reconstruction of Kaplan-Meier survival data
desc: Reconstructing participant-level data from published Kaplan-Meier curves supports meta-analysis and other secondary survival analyses when original trial records are unavailable. Researchers may use original PDF figures or screenshots, which can look alike but retain different information. We assessed how converting vector figures to images affects reconstruction by a language model that can inspect files and execute code. We generated 64 independent two-arm datasets across four scenarios combining 100 or 1,000 participants per arm with proportional or crossing hazards. Each figure was supplied as a native vector PDF and a matched 300-dpi PNG to Opus 5.5 through Claude Code under the same instructions. Outcomes compared reconstructed records with the original observed records: time-averaged absolute curve error through 24 months, error in the between-group restricted mean survival time difference, and error in the Cox log-hazard ratio. Native PDFs had lower curve error in all 64 completed pairs, including replacements for incomplete runs. Mean errors were 0.000029 and 0.1047 percentage points for PDF and PNG, respectively; the paired difference was -0.1047 (95% confidence interval, -0.1194 to -0.0909). PNG errors in the restricted mean survival time difference and log-hazard ratio were small: mean absolute errors were 0.0084 months and 0.0027. Lower resolution and compression increased curve errors; embedding unchanged pixels in a PDF did not restore vector accuracy. Some PNG runs exceeded the instructed revision limit, so results describe the implemented workflow rather than performance under a strictly enforced limit. Preserving vector information improved reconstruction fidelity in this workflow, but the observed differences do not establish clinically consequential changes in treatment estimates. Validation against reported survival summaries and event counts remains necessary. Generalization to published clinical figures and other model workflows requires further evaluation.

title: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
desc: [Frontiers in cardiovascular medicine] Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation. A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations. Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance. AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

title: High-Tech, High-Touch
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Touro University, California; conditions: Stress (Psychology), Resilience, Psychological, Anxiety, Depressive Symptoms, Well-being; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 43; status: COMPLETED] Medical students often experience high levels of stress, anxiety, and poor sleep, especially during their first year and around exams. This study looked at whether adding hands-on osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) to a wellness program built around a wearable ring and an artificial intelligence (AI) health coaching app could help first-year medical students. Forty-three first-year osteopathic medical students at one college took part. Each student was randomly assigned, by chance rather than by choice, to one of three groups for 23 weeks: a wearable ring alone; a wearable ring plus an AI health coaching app; or a wearable ring, the AI health coaching app, and seven OMT sessions given about every three weeks by osteopathic physicians. All students wore the ring daily. The ring recorded information such as sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability, which is a measure of how the nervous system responds to stress. Students also completed questionnaires about resilience and about symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress at three points: before the semester, in the middle, and at the end. Students answered additional surveys about their experience two months and seven months after the study ended. This was a small pilot study. Its main purpose was to find out whether a program like this can be carried out successfully and to gather the information needed to plan a larger study, rather than to determine whether OMT works. No harmful effects were reported.

title: COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels
desc: Machine-learning models based on routine laboratory panels can predict outcomes but can be difficult to interpret and operationalize. We present COMBIO, an automated pipeline that distils such a model into a compact closed-form biomarker. The composite is a product of laboratory measurements raised to integer powers from minus two to two. The sign of each exponent indicates whether higher values of the corresponding measurement increase or decrease the composite. Shapley additive explanation values from the gradient-boosted reference model rank five candidate measurements and guide eligible exponent signs. An exhaustive search over small integer exponents selects the formula on an inner validation set, before evaluation on the reserved test set. We evaluated COMBIO across six tasks: three National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey outcomes, liver-disease classification in the Indian Liver Patient Dataset, and Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV in-hospital mortality and sepsis case-finding, with external evaluation in the eICU Collaborative Research Database for the two hospital tasks. Across the six test sets, COMBIO's area under the receiver operating characteristic curve differed by at most 0.03 from logistic regression using the five candidate laboratory measurements. The hospital mortality composite had an area under the curve of 0.698 in the external database. A version restricted to widely available measurements in the source hospital database achieved an area under the curve of 0.786 in a cohort covering 92% of admissions. The multiplicative representation provides compactness rather than additional accuracy, and local validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

title: Deep learning screening of otoscopic images for ENT referral: development, validation and deployment of NHREF OtoScan
desc: Background. Middle and external ear disease is common and largely treatable, but accurate otoscopic interpretation requires training that is scarce outside specialist ENT services. Published deep learning models for otoscopy report high accuracy, yet most are optimised for closed set classification rather than the referral decision a non specialist actually makes, report uncalibrated probabilities, and do not report the near duplicate controls that video derived otoscopic datasets demand. We developed, validated and deployed a screening aid framed around referral rather than diagnosis. Methods. We merged 4,763 otoscopic images from 16 folders across three public datasets into 12 clinically meaningful classes. Every image was passed through a single field of view normalisation function (crop to the illuminated field, square, resize to 224 px, mask to one fixed circle) shared identically by training and inference, to remove the framing cue that otherwise identifies the source dataset. Because one source is video derived, images were grouped by cosine similarity of generic ImageNet features (threshold 0.93, joined transitively) and whole groups assigned to a single split, giving 3,326 training, 719 validation and 718 test images. A MobileNetV2 backbone initialised from ImageNet was fine tuned from block9expand. Probabilities were averaged over the eight dihedral transforms of each image and temperature scaled. The referral score was one minus the probability of a normal ear, and its threshold was set on the validation abnormal ears as the highest value still meeting a target sensitivity of 97%, applied with an inclusive comparison. Model selection, calibration and threshold were frozen before the test split was scored once. Results. On the 718 held out test images, referral sensitivity was 97.0% (95% CI 95.1 to 98.2) and specificity 75.6% (95% CI 69.4 to 80.8), with AUROC 0.974 for abnormal versus normal; a cluster bootstrap over the 363 similarity groups in the test split widens those intervals to 93.8 99.6% and 66.0 83.4% respectively. Of 501 abnormal ears, 15 were not referred; 11 of these were myringosclerosis and none was cholesteatoma. Twelve class macro F1 was 0.686, balanced accuracy 68.3%, and accuracy 85.0% (86.2% with chronic subtypes merged). Temperature scaling (T = 1.2) reduced expected calibration error from 0.0498 to 0.0430. A low confidence flag fired on 4.0% of test images, separating 87.2% accuracy on unflagged from 31.0% on flagged cases.
